# Data

## Loading NOAA Storm Events

Three NOAA Storm Events file types are loaded: event **details**, **fatalities**, and **locations**. Each is stored as a gzipped CSV in `data_dir` and discovered via `list.files()`. All matching files are loaded and row-bound in a single `purrr::map_df()` call.

```{r}
#| label: load_noaa_data

details_files    <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "StormEvents_details-ftp_v1.0_d.*\\.csv\\.gz$",   full.names = TRUE)
fatalities_files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "StormEvents_fatalities-ftp_v1.0_d.*\\.csv\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE)
locations_files  <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "StormEvents_locations-ftp_v1.0_d.*\\.csv\\.gz$",  full.names = TRUE)

storm_details    <- map_df(details_files,    read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
storm_fatalities <- map_df(fatalities_files, read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
storm_locations  <- map_df(locations_files,  read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Combining and Filtering to North Carolina

The three tables are joined on `EVENT_ID` using left joins, then filtered to North Carolina. A few administrative columns are dropped. Note that these joins can generate multiple rows per `EVENT_ID` — duplicates are resolved in the [Deduplication] step.

```{r}
#| label: combine_filter_nc

storm_combined <- storm_details %>%
  left_join(storm_fatalities, by = "EVENT_ID") %>%
  left_join(storm_locations,  by = "EVENT_ID")

nc_storm_combined <- storm_combined %>%
  filter(toupper(STATE) == "NORTH CAROLINA") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("STATE_FIPS", "CZ_TIMEZONE", "DATA_SOURCE")))

glimpse(nc_storm_combined)
```

# Methods

## Region Assignment

> **Why FIPS codes?** NOAA Storm Events records come in two types: **county-based** (`CZ_TYPE = "C"`) and **forecast-zone-based** (`CZ_TYPE = "Z"`). Matching on county *name strings* only captures county events. Zone-based events — which include large-area storms like Hurricane Helene — use NWS forecast zone names (e.g., *"Avery and Mitchell"*) that never match a plain county-name lookup. This analysis uses a **two-pass strategy**: (1) exact 3-digit county FIPS matching for county events, then (2) county-name keyword matching against zone names for zone events via `coalesce()`.

### Building Region Lookups

Two objects are constructed here and shared with the assignment chunk below:

- `nc_fips_region` — a 100-row tibble mapping every NC county's 3-digit FIPS code to its region.
- `assign_zone_region()` — a vectorized function that scans a zone name string for county-name and geographic keywords and returns the matching region. Word boundaries (`\b`) prevent partial-string false matches.

```{r}
#| label: build_region_lookups
#| echo: true

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# nc_fips_region: all 100 NC counties mapped by 3-digit county FIPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
nc_fips_region <- tibble(
  CZ_FIPS_NUM = c(
    # Mountains (24 counties)
    3, 5, 9, 11, 21, 23, 27, 39, 43, 75, 87, 89, 99,
    111, 113, 115, 121, 149, 161, 173, 175, 189, 193, 199,
    # Central (35 counties)
    1, 7, 25, 33, 35, 37, 45, 57, 59, 63, 67, 69, 71, 77, 81,
    97, 105, 109, 119, 123, 125, 135, 145, 151, 153, 157, 159,
    167, 169, 171, 179, 181, 183, 185, 197,
    # Coastal (41 counties)
    13, 15, 17, 19, 29, 31, 41, 47, 49, 51, 53, 55, 61, 65,
    73, 79, 83, 85, 91, 93, 95, 101, 103, 107, 117, 127, 129,
    131, 133, 137, 139, 141, 143, 147, 155, 163, 165, 177, 187,
    191, 195
  ),
  REGION = c(
    rep("mountains", 24),
    rep("central",   35),
    rep("coastal",   41)
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# assign_zone_region(): keyword-based region inference for zone events
# Priority order: mountains → coastal → central
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
assign_zone_region <- function(cz_name) {
  z <- toupper(trimws(as.character(cz_name)))

  mountain_re <- paste(c(
    "\\bALEXANDER\\b", "\\bALLEGHANY\\b", "\\bASHE\\b",    "\\bAVERY\\b",
    "\\bBUNCOMBE\\b",  "\\bBURKE\\b",      "\\bCALDWELL\\b","\\bCHEROKEE\\b",
    "\\bCLAY\\b",      "\\bGRAHAM\\b",     "\\bHAYWOOD\\b", "\\bHENDERSON\\b",
    "\\bJACKSON\\b",   "\\bMCDOWELL\\b",   "\\bMACON\\b",   "\\bMADISON\\b",
    "\\bMITCHELL\\b",  "\\bPOLK\\b",       "\\bRUTHERFORD\\b", "\\bSWAIN\\b",
    "\\bTRANSYLVANIA\\b", "\\bWATAUGA\\b", "\\bWILKES\\b",  "\\bYANCEY\\b",
    "MOUNTAIN", "BLUE RIDGE", "HIGHLAND", "FOOTHIL"
  ), collapse = "|")

  coastal_re <- paste(c(
    "\\bBEAUFORT\\b",   "\\bBERTIE\\b",     "\\bBLADEN\\b",     "\\bBRUNSWICK\\b",
    "\\bCAMDEN\\b",     "\\bCARTERET\\b",   "\\bCHOWAN\\b",     "\\bCOLUMBUS\\b",
    "\\bCRAVEN\\b",     "\\bCUMBERLAND\\b", "\\bCURRITUCK\\b",  "\\bDARE\\b",
    "\\bDUPLIN\\b",     "\\bEDGECOMBE\\b",  "\\bGATES\\b",      "\\bGREENE\\b",
    "\\bHALIFAX\\b",    "\\bHARNETT\\b",    "\\bHERTFORD\\b",   "\\bHOKE\\b",
    "\\bHYDE\\b",       "\\bJOHNSTON\\b",   "\\bJONES\\b",      "\\bLENOIR\\b",
    "\\bMARTIN\\b",     "\\bNASH\\b",        "NEW HANOVER",     "\\bNORTHAMPTON\\b",
    "\\bONSLOW\\b",     "\\bPAMLICO\\b",    "\\bPASQUOTANK\\b", "\\bPENDER\\b",
    "\\bPERQUIMANS\\b", "\\bPITT\\b",       "\\bROBESON\\b",    "\\bSAMPSON\\b",
    "\\bSCOTLAND\\b",   "\\bTYRRELL\\b",    "\\bWASHINGTON\\b", "\\bWAYNE\\b",
    "\\bWILSON\\b",     "COASTAL", "TIDEWATER", "OUTER BANK", "\\bSOUND\\b"
  ), collapse = "|")

  central_re <- paste(c(
    "\\bALAMANCE\\b",  "\\bANSON\\b",      "\\bCABARRUS\\b",   "\\bCASWELL\\b",
    "\\bCATAWBA\\b",   "\\bCHATHAM\\b",    "\\bCLEVELAND\\b",  "\\bDAVIDSON\\b",
    "\\bDAVIE\\b",     "\\bDURHAM\\b",     "\\bFORSYTH\\b",    "\\bFRANKLIN\\b",
    "\\bGASTON\\b",    "\\bGRANVILLE\\b",  "\\bGUILFORD\\b",   "\\bIREDELL\\b",
    "\\bLEE\\b",       "\\bLINCOLN\\b",    "\\bMECKLENBURG\\b","\\bMONTGOMERY\\b",
    "\\bMOORE\\b",     "\\bORANGE\\b",     "\\bPERSON\\b",     "\\bRANDOLPH\\b",
    "\\bRICHMOND\\b",  "\\bROCKINGHAM\\b", "\\bROWAN\\b",      "\\bSTANLY\\b",
    "\\bSTOKES\\b",    "\\bSURRY\\b",      "\\bUNION\\b",      "\\bVANCE\\b",
    "\\bWAKE\\b",      "\\bWARREN\\b",     "\\bYADKIN\\b",
    "PIEDMONT", "\\bTRIAD\\b", "\\bTRIANGLE\\b", "METROLINA", "SANDHILLS"
  ), collapse = "|")

  case_when(
    is.na(cz_name)             ~ NA_character_,
    str_detect(z, mountain_re) ~ "mountains",
    str_detect(z, coastal_re)  ~ "coastal",
    str_detect(z, central_re)  ~ "central",
    TRUE                       ~ NA_character_
  )
}
```

### Assigning Regions

County events (`CZ_TYPE = "C"`) are matched via FIPS join. Zone and marine events use `assign_zone_region()` as a fallback via `coalesce()`. The `%% 1000L` operation extracts the 3-digit county code from either a 3-digit ("003") or 5-digit ("37003") FIPS string. The count table below shows how many rows landed in each region after both passes.

```{r}
#| label: assign_nc_regions
#| echo: true

nc_storm_combined <- nc_storm_combined %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract 3-digit county FIPS; zone events get NA so the FIPS join skips them
    CZ_FIPS_NUM = suppressWarnings(
      if_else(
        toupper(trimws(as.character(CZ_TYPE))) == "C",
        as.integer(CZ_FIPS) %% 1000L,
        NA_integer_
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  # Pass 1: exact FIPS match for county events
  left_join(nc_fips_region, by = "CZ_FIPS_NUM") %>%
  mutate(
    # Pass 2: keyword match for zone events where FIPS gave NA
    REGION = coalesce(
      REGION,
      assign_zone_region(toupper(trimws(as.character(CZ_NAME))))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-CZ_FIPS_NUM)

# Region coverage (NA = event fell outside all region definitions)
table(nc_storm_combined$REGION, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Data Processing

### Helper Functions

Four utility functions support the downstream analysis. `parse_noaa_damage()` converts NOAA compact damage strings (e.g., `"10.00K"`, `"2.50M"`) to numeric dollar amounts. The remaining three handle aggregation edge cases: returning the first non-missing value, computing a safe maximum, and applying a log-scaled 0–100 rescaling.

```{r}
#| label: helper_functions
#| echo: true

# parse_noaa_damage(): "10K" → 10000, "2.5M" → 2500000, "1B" → 1000000000
parse_noaa_damage <- function(x, missing_value = 0) {
  x_clean <- toupper(trimws(as.character(x)))
  result <- case_when(
    is.na(x_clean) | x_clean %in% c("", "NA", "NULL") ~ missing_value,
    str_detect(x_clean, "B$") ~ parse_number(x_clean) * 1e9,
    str_detect(x_clean, "M$") ~ parse_number(x_clean) * 1e6,
    str_detect(x_clean, "K$") ~ parse_number(x_clean) * 1e3,
    TRUE                       ~ parse_number(x_clean)
  )
  replace_na(result, missing_value)
}

# first_nonmissing(): returns the first non-NA, non-blank value in a vector
first_nonmissing <- function(x, default = NA) {
  valid_values <- x[!is.na(x) & !(is.character(x) & trimws(x) == "")]
  if (length(valid_values) == 0) return(default)
  valid_values[[1]]
}

# max_or_zero(): safe maximum, treating NA as 0
# Used to prevent double-counting repeated event-level values after joins
max_or_zero <- function(x, default = 0) {
  x_num <- replace_na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)), default)
  if (length(x_num) == 0) return(default)
  max(x_num, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# rescale_log(): log1p-transform then linearly rescale to output_range
rescale_log <- function(x, output_range = c(0, 100)) {
  x     <- replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  x_log <- log1p(x)
  if (length(x_log) == 0 || diff(range(x_log, na.rm = TRUE)) == 0) {
    return(rep(output_range[1], length(x_log)))
  }
  scales::rescale(x_log, to = output_range)
}
```

### Cleaning Storm Records

Text fields are standardized, numeric columns are coerced, and NOAA damage strings are converted to dollars. `across()` applies the same transformation to all four human-impact columns at once. Records missing `EVENT_ID` / `EVENT_TYPE`, or falling outside the three named regions, are dropped.

```{r}
#| label: clean_storm_data
#| echo: true

storm_clean <- nc_storm_combined %>%
  mutate(
    EVENT_TYPE = replace_na(str_squish(as.character(EVENT_TYPE)), "Unknown"),
    REGION     = str_to_lower(str_squish(as.character(REGION))),
    across(
      c(INJURIES_DIRECT, INJURIES_INDIRECT, DEATHS_DIRECT, DEATHS_INDIRECT),
      ~ replace_na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)), 0)
    ),
    PROPERTY_DAMAGE_DOLLARS = parse_noaa_damage(DAMAGE_PROPERTY),
    CROP_DAMAGE_DOLLARS     = parse_noaa_damage(DAMAGE_CROPS)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(EVENT_ID),
    !is.na(EVENT_TYPE),
    REGION %in% c("mountains", "central", "coastal")
  )
```

### Deduplication {#deduplication}

The fatality and location joins can produce multiple rows per `EVENT_ID`. The data are collapsed to one record per `EVENT_ID` × `REGION` pair using `max_or_zero()`, which selects the true event-level value rather than summing a potentially repeated entry. `across()` applies `max_or_zero()` to all six impact columns simultaneously. A verification check confirms no duplicate pairs remain.

```{r}
#| label: deduplicate_storm_records
#| echo: true

storm_event_region <- storm_clean %>%
  group_by(EVENT_ID, REGION) %>%
  summarise(
    EVENT_TYPE = first_nonmissing(EVENT_TYPE),
    YEAR       = first_nonmissing(YEAR),
    MONTH_NAME = first_nonmissing(MONTH_NAME),
    CZ_NAME    = first_nonmissing(CZ_NAME),
    across(
      c(INJURIES_DIRECT, INJURIES_INDIRECT,
        DEATHS_DIRECT,   DEATHS_INDIRECT,
        PROPERTY_DAMAGE_DOLLARS, CROP_DAMAGE_DOLLARS),
      max_or_zero
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    TOTAL_INJURIES = INJURIES_DIRECT + INJURIES_INDIRECT,
    TOTAL_DEATHS   = DEATHS_DIRECT   + DEATHS_INDIRECT,
    TOTAL_DAMAGE   = PROPERTY_DAMAGE_DOLLARS + CROP_DAMAGE_DOLLARS
  )

# Verification: each EVENT_ID × REGION pair should appear exactly once
storm_event_region %>%
  count(EVENT_ID, REGION) %>%
  summarise(
    max_rows_per_pair = max(n),
    duplicate_pairs   = sum(n > 1)
  )
```

## Analysis

### Regional Impact Summary

The deduplicated records are aggregated by `REGION` and `EVENT_TYPE` to produce totals and per-event rates for all impact metrics.

```{r}
#| label: summarize_regional_impacts
#| echo: true

regional_impacts <- storm_event_region %>%
  group_by(REGION, EVENT_TYPE) %>%
  summarise(
    EVENTS          = n(),
    INJURIES        = sum(TOTAL_INJURIES,         na.rm = TRUE),
    DEATHS          = sum(TOTAL_DEATHS,           na.rm = TRUE),
    PROPERTY_DAMAGE = sum(PROPERTY_DAMAGE_DOLLARS, na.rm = TRUE),
    CROP_DAMAGE     = sum(CROP_DAMAGE_DOLLARS,     na.rm = TRUE),
    TOTAL_DAMAGE    = sum(TOTAL_DAMAGE,            na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    DAMAGE_PER_EVENT   = TOTAL_DAMAGE / EVENTS,
    INJURIES_PER_EVENT = INJURIES     / EVENTS,
    DEATHS_PER_EVENT   = DEATHS       / EVENTS
  )
```

### Composite Impact Score

A single 0–100 composite score summarizes each impact dimension. Each dimension is log-transformed and rescaled to [0, 100] before being combined using the weights below. Weights must sum to 1 and are adjustable via the function arguments.

| Dimension        | Default Weight |
|------------------|---------------|
| Economic damage  | 50%           |
| Injuries         | 30%           |
| Deaths           | 20%           |

```{r}
#| label: impact_score_function
#| echo: true

calculate_impact_scores <- function(
    data,
    damage_weight = 0.50,
    injury_weight = 0.30,
    death_weight  = 0.20,
    score_min     = 0,
    score_max     = 100
) {
  if (abs(damage_weight + injury_weight + death_weight - 1) > 0.001) {
    stop("damage_weight, injury_weight, and death_weight must sum to 1.")
  }
  data %>%
    mutate(
      DAMAGE_SCORE = rescale_log(TOTAL_DAMAGE, output_range = c(score_min, score_max)),
      INJURY_SCORE = rescale_log(INJURIES,     output_range = c(score_min, score_max)),
      DEATH_SCORE  = rescale_log(DEATHS,       output_range = c(score_min, score_max)),
      IMPACT_SCORE = damage_weight * DAMAGE_SCORE +
                     injury_weight * INJURY_SCORE +
                     death_weight  * DEATH_SCORE
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: apply_impact_scores
#| echo: true

regional_impacts_scored <- calculate_impact_scores(
  regional_impacts,
  damage_weight = 0.50,
  injury_weight = 0.30,
  death_weight  = 0.20
)

# top_event_types: shared across Figures 2, 3, and 5
top_n_event_types <- 15

top_event_types <- regional_impacts_scored %>%
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE) %>%
  summarise(OVERALL_IMPACT = sum(IMPACT_SCORE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(order_by = OVERALL_IMPACT, n = top_n_event_types, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(EVENT_TYPE)

# overall_event_impact: shared across Figure 4 and the Key Results table
overall_event_impact <- regional_impacts_scored %>%
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE) %>%
  summarise(
    OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE = sum(IMPACT_SCORE, na.rm = TRUE),
    TOTAL_EVENTS         = sum(EVENTS,       na.rm = TRUE),
    TOTAL_INJURIES       = sum(INJURIES,     na.rm = TRUE),
    TOTAL_DEATHS         = sum(DEATHS,       na.rm = TRUE),
    TOTAL_DAMAGE         = sum(TOTAL_DAMAGE, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups              = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE))
```

# Results

The figures below summarize storm frequency, composite impact, and individual impact components across North Carolina's three geographic regions: **Mountains**, **Central**, and **Coastal**.

## Figure 1 — Event Frequency by Region

The 15 most frequently recorded storm event types are shown for each region. Counts reflect the deduplicated event–region dataset.

```{r}
#| label: figure_event_counts
#| echo: true
#| fig-height: 14

event_counts <- storm_event_region %>%
  count(REGION, EVENT_TYPE, name = "EVENTS") %>%
  mutate(
    REGION = factor(
      REGION,
      levels = c("mountains", "central", "coastal"),
      labels = c("Mountains", "Central", "Coastal")
    )
  )

plot_event_counts_by_region <- function(data, region_name, fill_color, top_n = 15) {
  data %>%
    filter(REGION == region_name) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = EVENTS, n = top_n, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(EVENT_TYPE = fct_reorder(EVENT_TYPE, EVENTS)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = EVENT_TYPE, y = EVENTS)) +
    geom_col(fill = fill_color) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
    labs(title = region_name, x = NULL, y = "Number of Events") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
    )
}

p_events_mountains <- plot_event_counts_by_region(event_counts, "Mountains", "#2E8B57")
p_events_central   <- plot_event_counts_by_region(event_counts, "Central",   "#CD5C5C")
p_events_coastal   <- plot_event_counts_by_region(event_counts, "Coastal",   "#4682B4")

event_count_figure <- (p_events_mountains / p_events_central / p_events_coastal) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Storm Event Frequency Across North Carolina Regions",
    subtitle = "Top storm event types by number of recorded events",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 17, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30")
    )
  )

event_count_figure

ggsave(
  filename = "nc_storm_event_counts_by_region.png",
  plot     = event_count_figure,
  path     = results_dir,
  width    = 24, height = 28, units = "cm", dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure 2 — Composite Storm Impact

The heatmap displays composite impact scores for the top `r top_n_event_types` event types across all three regions. Scores range from 0 to 100 and combine log-rescaled damage, injury, and death metrics.

```{r}
#| label: figure_composite_heatmap
#| echo: true

heatmap_data <- regional_impacts_scored %>%
  filter(EVENT_TYPE %in% top_event_types) %>%
  mutate(
    REGION = factor(
      REGION,
      levels = c("mountains", "central", "coastal"),
      labels = c("Mountains", "Central", "Coastal")
    ),
    EVENT_TYPE = factor(EVENT_TYPE, levels = rev(top_event_types))
  )

plot_impact_heatmap <- function(
    data,
    value_column = IMPACT_SCORE,
    title        = "Storm Impact by Event Type and Region",
    subtitle     = "Higher scores indicate greater combined impacts",
    low_color    = "#F7FBFF",
    high_color   = "#B2182B",
    show_values  = TRUE,
    value_digits = 1
) {
  value_col <- rlang::enquo(value_column)

  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = EVENT_TYPE, y = REGION, fill = !!value_col)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low    = low_color, high   = high_color,
      limits = c(0, 100), breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100),
      name   = "Impact Score"
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = "Storm Event Type", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
      plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "gray30"),
      axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      axis.text.y     = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid      = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "right"
    )

  if (show_values) {
    p <- p + geom_text(
      aes(label = round(!!value_col, value_digits)),
      size = 3, color = "black"
    )
  }
  p
}

p_composite_heatmap <- plot_impact_heatmap(
  data         = heatmap_data,
  value_column = IMPACT_SCORE,
  title        = "Storm Impact by Event Type and North Carolina Region",
  subtitle     = "Composite score combines damage, injuries, and deaths; scores range from 0 to 100",
  low_color    = "#F7FBFF",
  high_color   = "#B2182B"
)

p_composite_heatmap

ggsave(
  filename = "nc_storm_composite_impact_heatmap.png",
  plot     = p_composite_heatmap,
  path     = results_dir,
  width    = 16, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure 3 — Impact Components by Region

Each panel isolates one impact dimension across the top event types and three regions. A logarithmic color scale is used because total damage values are orders of magnitude larger than injury or event counts.

```{r}
#| label: figure_impact_components
#| echo: true
#| fig-height: 10

component_data <- regional_impacts_scored %>%
  filter(EVENT_TYPE %in% top_event_types) %>%
  select(REGION, EVENT_TYPE, EVENTS, INJURIES, DEATHS, TOTAL_DAMAGE) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(EVENTS, INJURIES, DEATHS, TOTAL_DAMAGE),
    names_to  = "IMPACT_TYPE",
    values_to = "VALUE"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    REGION = factor(
      REGION,
      levels = c("mountains", "central", "coastal"),
      labels = c("Mountains", "Central", "Coastal")
    ),
    IMPACT_TYPE = factor(
      IMPACT_TYPE,
      levels = c("EVENTS", "INJURIES", "DEATHS", "TOTAL_DAMAGE"),
      labels = c("Number of Events", "Injuries", "Deaths", "Total Damage")
    ),
    EVENT_TYPE = factor(EVENT_TYPE, levels = rev(top_event_types))
  )

p_component_heatmaps <- ggplot(
  component_data,
  aes(x = EVENT_TYPE, y = REGION, fill = VALUE)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ IMPACT_TYPE, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "C", trans = "log1p",
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ",", scale_cut = cut_short_scale()),
    name   = "Reported Value"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Storm Impact Components by Event Type and Region",
    subtitle = "Darker cells indicate larger reported values; color scale is logarithmic",
    x        = "Storm Event Type", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30"),
    axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y   = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid    = element_blank(),
    strip.text    = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p_component_heatmaps

ggsave(
  filename = "nc_storm_impact_components_by_region.png",
  plot     = p_component_heatmaps,
  path     = results_dir,
  width    = 16, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure 4 — Overall Impact Ranking

Composite scores are summed across all three regions to rank event types statewide. This collapses regional variation to highlight the highest-burden event types across North Carolina.

```{r}
#| label: figure_overall_impact_ranking
#| echo: true

plot_overall_impact <- function(data, top_n = 15, fill_low = "#D9F0D3", fill_high = "#B2182B") {
  data %>%
    slice_max(order_by = OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE, n = top_n, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(EVENT_TYPE = fct_reorder(EVENT_TYPE, OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = EVENT_TYPE, y = OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE, fill = OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE)) +
    geom_col() +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = fill_low, high = fill_high, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +
    labs(
      title    = "Overall Storm Impact by Event Type",
      subtitle = "Impact scores summed across the Mountains, Central, and Coastal regions",
      x        = NULL,
      y        = "Summed Composite Impact Score"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = "gray30"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
    )
}

p_overall_impact <- plot_overall_impact(data = overall_event_impact, top_n = 15)
p_overall_impact

ggsave(
  filename = "nc_storm_overall_impact_by_event_type.png",
  plot     = p_overall_impact,
  path     = results_dir,
  width    = 12, height = 9, units = "in", dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure 6 — Economic Damage by Region

Property and crop damage are shown separately for each region, in millions of dollars, aggregated across all recorded storm events.

```{r}
#| label: figure_damage_by_region
#| echo: true

damage_by_region <- regional_impacts_scored %>%
  group_by(REGION) %>%
  summarise(
    PROPERTY_DAMAGE = sum(PROPERTY_DAMAGE, na.rm = TRUE),
    CROP_DAMAGE     = sum(CROP_DAMAGE,     na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    REGION = factor(
      REGION,
      levels = c("mountains", "central", "coastal"),
      labels = c("Mountains", "Central", "Coastal")
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(PROPERTY_DAMAGE, CROP_DAMAGE),
    names_to  = "DAMAGE_TYPE",
    values_to = "DAMAGE"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    DAMAGE_TYPE = recode(
      DAMAGE_TYPE,
      PROPERTY_DAMAGE = "Property Damage",
      CROP_DAMAGE     = "Crop Damage"
    )
  )

p_damage_by_region <- ggplot(damage_by_region, aes(x = REGION, y = DAMAGE, fill = DAMAGE_TYPE)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Property Damage" = "#8C2D04", "Crop Damage" = "#31A354")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Reported Property and Crop Damage by Region",
    subtitle = "Aggregate NOAA damage estimates across all recorded storm events",
    x        = NULL, y = "Damage (millions of dollars)", fill = "Damage Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "gray30"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_damage_by_region

ggsave(
  filename = "nc_storm_damage_by_region.png",

  path     = results_dir,

)
```

Total storm-related injuries and deaths are compared across the three regions, drawn from NOAA storm event records.


## Key Results

### Top Event Types by Overall Impact

The 10 highest-impact event types statewide, ranked by summed composite score across all three regions.

```{r}
#| label: results_top_event_types
#| echo: true

format_damage <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x >= 1e9 ~ paste0("$", round(x / 1e9, 1), "B"),
    x >= 1e6 ~ paste0("$", round(x / 1e6, 1), "M"),
    x >= 1e3 ~ paste0("$", round(x / 1e3, 0), "K"),
    TRUE     ~ paste0("$", round(x, 0))
  )
}

overall_event_impact %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(
    OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE = round(OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE, 1),
    TOTAL_DAMAGE         = format_damage(TOTAL_DAMAGE)
  ) %>%
  rename(
    "Event Type"          = EVENT_TYPE,
    "Impact Score"        = OVERALL_IMPACT_SCORE,
    "Total Events"        = TOTAL_EVENTS,
    "Total Injuries"      = TOTAL_INJURIES,
    "Total Deaths"        = TOTAL_DEATHS,
    "Total Damage (Est.)" = TOTAL_DAMAGE
  ) %>%
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = FALSE,
    class    = "display compact",
    options  = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
  )
```

### Top Region × Event Combinations

The 15 highest-scoring region × event type combinations, preserving the geographic breakdown.

```{r}
#| label: results_top_region_combos
#| echo: true

regional_impacts_scored %>%
  arrange(desc(IMPACT_SCORE)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  select(REGION, EVENT_TYPE, IMPACT_SCORE, EVENTS, INJURIES, DEATHS, TOTAL_DAMAGE) %>%
  mutate(
    REGION       = str_to_title(REGION),
    IMPACT_SCORE = round(IMPACT_SCORE, 1),
    TOTAL_DAMAGE = format_damage(TOTAL_DAMAGE)
  ) %>%
  rename(
    "Region"              = REGION,
    "Event Type"          = EVENT_TYPE,
    "Impact Score"        = IMPACT_SCORE,
    "Events"              = EVENTS,
    "Injuries"            = INJURIES,
    "Deaths"              = DEATHS,
    "Total Damage (Est.)" = TOTAL_DAMAGE
  ) %>%
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = FALSE,
    class    = "display compact",
    options  = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE)
  )
```
